record.title: Anthropic launches Cyber Mission for critical infrastructure and open-source security
record.summary: Anthropic announced a Cyber Mission on October 8 with two initial programs: a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program that pairs frontier Claude models, on-site engineers and threat research with trusted providers, and OSS Scanner, an opt-in service offering periodic model-generated vulnerability reports to open-source projects without human review. Anthropic names 11 founding infrastructure partners and says several are already working with Claude on vulnerabilities and customer fixes. Dragos separately confirms its participation and says it plans to develop detections, engineering guidance and shared knowledge through the program; it reports no completed outcome. It expects OSS Scanner’s true-positive rate to exceed 90%, while acknowledging that reports may contain errors such as incorrect severity ratings. Anthropic says projects must be able to triage the findings and that it will continue human-verified coordinated disclosures for others. These are company-reported program details and expectations; no independent scanner audit, adoption measure, or net risk reduction was inspected. The linked program documentation adds operating boundaries: projects are manually checked for core-maintainer status, unvalidated scanner reports do not start a 90-day disclosure period, and only findings later validated through Anthropic’s human-reviewed CVD process may do so. Anthropic says its scan agents run without internet access in hardened sandboxes and reports are kept in a restricted cloud project; these are provider-described safeguards, not an independent security audit.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic announced a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program pairing Claude models, on-site engineers and threat research with trusted providers; it named 11 founding partners and says work with several partners is underway.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Anthropic launched an opt-in OSS Scanner that sends periodic, free, model-generated vulnerability reports to enrolled projects without human review; Anthropic says the service is for projects able to triage findings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic expects OSS Scanner's true-positive rate to exceed 90%, while acknowledging that some reports may contain errors; this is a provider forecast, not an independently audited rate.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The announcement does not establish independent scanner accuracy, adoption, patch outcomes, or net reduction in cyber risk.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Dragos separately confirms that it joined the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program and says it intends to turn program learning into improved detections, engineering guidance and shared knowledge; no completed program outcome is reported.

claims.label: CLAIMED_PROVIDER_OPERATING_TERMS
claims.text: Anthropic’s OSS Scanner documentation says enrollment is opt-in and limited to projects whose core maintainers are manually checked; unvalidated model reports do not start a 90-day disclosure period, while reports later human-validated through the existing CVD process may be disclosed 90 days after notification. Anthropic also describes isolated report storage and scanning agents in hardened, internet-disabled sandboxes.

evidence_gaps.description: The expected scanner true-positive rate, severity accuracy, fix quality and maintainer burden have no independent audit in the inspected evidence.
No comparative evidence shows whether the programs improve patch speed or reduce cyber risk at scale.

brief.importance_rationale: If the announced programs make frontier-model security work and engineering capacity available to critical-infrastructure providers and maintainers at useful scale, they could affect vulnerability discovery and remediation across consequential systems. Consequence is significant, but the launch does not establish independent scanner accuracy, net risk reduction, or broad deployment outcomes.
limitations: All effectiveness, partner progress and >90% true-positive claims are Anthropic-reported and were not independently audited.
OSS Scanner reports are sent without human review and may contain incorrect details; Anthropic says the service is aimed at projects able to triage findings.
The announcement provides no independent adoption, patch-rate, vulnerability-severity, time-to-fix, or net-risk-reduction comparison.
No scanner output or sensitive vulnerability details were accessed in this review.

The OSS Scanner terms, enrollment checks, report handling and sandbox/security practices are provider descriptions; this activation did not inspect the implementation or independently audit data isolation, model accuracy, disclosure outcomes or maintainer burden.

technical.claimed_result: Anthropic says several CIDP partners are already using Claude to fix vulnerabilities and help customers do the same; it expects OSS Scanner true positives above 90%. No independent outcome or accuracy measurement was inspected. Dragos says it intends to turn program learning into better detections, engineering guidance and shared knowledge; it reports no completed result.
technical.demonstrated_result: Anthropic published program descriptions, named 11 founding CIDP partners, and opened an opt-in OSS Scanner. These establish the announced offering, not its effectiveness. Dragos independently confirms its own participation. The linked Anthropic OSS Scanner page specifies opt-in enrollment, manual core-maintainer checks, periodic scans, and a disclosure policy that does not impose a 90-day period on unvalidated model reports; the page describes human validation before a later CVD period and states that agents run in hardened sandboxes without internet access. These are published provider terms and descriptions, not independently audited implementation.
technical.implementation_status: Programs announced October 8; Anthropic says work is underway with several infrastructure partners. OSS Scanner is opt-in. Scale, adoption and operational outcomes remain unknown.
technical.mechanism: CIDP supplies Claude models, on-site engineers and threat research through trusted providers serving operational technology. OSS Scanner is an opt-in periodic scanning service: enrolled projects receive model-generated vulnerability reports, proof-of-concept, explanation and a suggested fix where available, without human review.
technical.regime: Anthropic-announced U.S.-anchored critical-infrastructure provider cohort and opt-in open-source projects capable of triaging reports. The launch does not describe coverage, independent validation, or achieved patch rates.
technical.reproducibility: The announcement supports the program terms and stated expectations. No scanner reports, independent audit set, partner metrics or reproduction were inspected. The service documentation describes enrollment, report handling and security controls but provides no audit artifact or independent operational evidence.
technical.strongest_baseline: Anthropic says its earlier Project Glasswing scanned hundreds of projects with humans triaging many findings; OSS Scanner changes this for enrolled projects by sending unreviewed model reports. No matched accuracy or remediation baseline was provided.

brief.title: Anthropic launches Cyber Mission for critical infrastructure and open-source security
brief.why_it_matters: The programs commit engineering support and frontier models to vulnerability discovery and repair in critical-infrastructure and open-source systems. Their value depends on finding actionable issues, protecting disclosure, and helping maintainers patch without overwhelming them. The announcement establishes program design and stated activity, not independently measured accuracy or reduced cyber risk.
